states.name: Bihar
states.history: Madhubani painting traces its roots to the ancient kingdom of Mithila, said to have originated when King Janaka commissioned artists to paint the grand wedding ceremony of his daughter Sita to Lord Rama.
states.significance: Traditionally painted on freshly plastered mud walls and floors during auspicious lifecycle events like Kohbar (wedding chambers), festivals like Chhath Puja, and harvests. Women passed down intricate geometric knowledge across generations.
facts: Traditionally divided into five distinct styles: Bharni, Katchni, Tantrik, Godna, and Kohbar.
Natural pigments were prepared from aparajita flowers, turmeric, indigo, soot, and bilva leaves.
Received prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) tag protecting authentic Mithila artisans.
materials: Handmade wasli paper soaked in cow-dung water

tutorial.title: Creating a Sacred Matsya (Fish) & Lotus Madhubani Motif
materials: A4 Cartridge paper or Handmade Paper
Watercolor / Acrylic paints (Yellow, Red, Blue, Green)

steps.title: Draw the Iconic Double-Line Border
steps.text: Draw a 1-inch border all around the paper using two parallel pencil lines 5mm apart. Madhubani art is never left unframed.

steps.title: Sketch the Matsya (Sacred Fish) Contour
steps.text: In the center, draw a graceful curved almond shape for the fish body. Extend two flowing curved fins at top and bottom, and a split fan tail at the rear.

steps.title: Divide Body into Geometric Compartments
steps.text: Divide the body of the fish using 3 to 4 vertical curved arches. Fill each section with fine parallel lines, dots, or small fish scales.

steps.title: Surround with Nature Motifs (No Empty Space)
steps.text: Traditional Mithila art abhors empty space (horror vacui). Fill all surrounding empty background with swirling water waves, lotus buds, flowers, and swimming fishes.

steps.title: Apply Flat Vibrant Colors (Bharni)
steps.text: Using bright crimson red, turmeric yellow, sap green, and deep indigo blue, color each segment smoothly with flat, unblended tones.

states.name: Andhra Pradesh
states.history: Kalamkari translates to "pen craft" (Kalam = pen, Kari = craftsmanship). Under the patronage of the Vijayanagara Empire, temple scrolls depicting epic narratives from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, and Puranas flourished around the Swarnamukhi river in Srikalahasti.
states.significance: Kalamkari scrolls served as visual teaching tools carried by wandering village bards (Katha-vachakas) who sang temple folklore to rural congregations. The entire process uses 17 organic wash and mordant stages.
facts: The Swarnamukhi river water is rich in specific minerals that react with myrobalan to yield deep indelible black and madder red dyes.
Artisans use buffalo milk washes to prevent the natural vegetable dyes from bleeding into adjacent cloth fibers.
Srikalahasti is one of the only surviving centers where pure freehand pen drawing is practiced without wooden blocks.
materials: Bamboo reed pen (Kalam) with sheep wool reservoir

tutorial.title: Painting Goddess Saraswati / Celestial Hamsa with Kalamkari Pen Technique
materials: Cotton canvas cloth or heavy cold-press watercolor paper
Burnt sienna, crimson red, ochre yellow, and indigo paints

steps.title: Base Wash & Sacred Proportioning
steps.text: Prepare your paper or fabric with a light wash of tea or coffee decoction to mimic the traditional sun-dried myrobalan cream base.

steps.title: Freehand Kalam Inking of Deity / Hamsa Motif
steps.text: Draw the sweeping arch of the celestial Swan (Hamsa) with a long curved neck, lotus eyes, and billowing ornamental plumage resembling temple temple gopuram motifs.

steps.title: Apply Black Kasim Linework
steps.text: Outline the temple jewelry, necklaces, mukuta crown, and the veena strings with bold black ink lines.

steps.title: Layer Natural Madder Red & Saffron Ochre
steps.text: Fill the background with deep crimson red or madder tones. Color the skin and ornamental halo with warm gold-yellow.

steps.title: Intricate Floral Border Finishing
steps.text: Border your painting with the iconic "Karru" creeper motif consisting of intertwining vines, buds, and miniature paisleys.

states.name: Maharashtra
states.history: Warli art is one of the oldest living tribal art forms in India, with roots dating back to the Neolithic period (2500-3000 BCE). Created by the Warli tribe residing on the Sahyadri mountains of northern Maharashtra.
states.significance: Warli paintings do not depict mythological deities; instead, they capture human harmony with mother nature (Mother Palghata), farming, hunting, rituals, and the iconic circular Tarpa dance celebrating cosmic time.
facts: Uses only three elementary geometric shapes: Circle (Sun & Moon), Triangle (Mountains & Conical Trees), and Square (Sacred Land & Palghat chowk).
The human figure is formed by two inverse triangles joined at the tip, symbolizing balance of physical and spiritual energies.
Traditionally painted exclusively by tribal women (Suhasinis) to consecrate wedding homes.
materials: Rice flour mixed with water and babool tree gum
Red ochre (Geru) and cow-dung mud wall base
Crushed bamboo stick chewed into a flexible brush
motifs: Sun and Crescent Moon (Eternal celestial witnesses)

tutorial.title: Painting the Warli Sacred Tree of Life & Community Dance
materials: Terracotta / Kraft brown paper or canvas board
White gel pen for fine lines

steps.title: Prepare the Mud-Ochre Canvas
steps.text: Paint your background with a warm terracotta or burnt sienna base coat to emulate traditional sun-dried village mud walls.

steps.title: Construct the Central Sacred Tree (Kalpavriksha)
steps.text: Draw a central vertical trunk in the middle. Sprout rhythmic triangular branches extending symmetrically outwards.

steps.title: Draw Warli Figures using Intersecting Triangles
steps.text: Draw a small circle for the head. Beneath it, draw an inverted triangle for the upper torso and an upright triangle for the hips meeting at the waist.

steps.title: Incorporate Forest Animals & Birds
steps.text: Paint spotted cattle, peacocks, deer, and monkeys resting amidst the branches. Decorate their bodies with white dots and fine line textures.

steps.title: Geometric Warli Border
steps.text: Frame the artwork with a border of alternating triangles, continuous spiral zig-zags, or linked dancing figures holding hands.

states.name: Rajasthan
states.history: Pichwai originated over 400 years ago in Nathdwara near Udaipur as devotional cloth backdrops hung behind the idol of Shrinathji (Lord Krishna). Rajasthani miniature painting schools (Mewar, Marwar, Kishangarh, Bundi) set the pinnacle of Indian courtly artistry.
states.significance: Pichwais reflect the changing seasons, festivals (Janmashtami, Sharad Purnima, Annakoot), and divine moods (Bhavas). Miniature paintings celebrated poetry (Rasikapriya, Gita Govinda) and royal processions with boundless splendor.
facts: Miniature masters use paintbrushes crafted from a single hair plucked from the tail of a living squirrel.
Pure gold and silver leaf (Zari / Vark) are ground with gum and burnished with agate stone to produce gleaming 3D jewelry.
A master-grade 6x4 foot Pichwai takes an entire family of master painters up to 6 months to complete.
materials: Starched khadi cloth or wasli paper

tutorial.title: Creating a Royal Kadamba Tree & Lotus Pichwai Artwork
materials: Stretched canvas board or heavy watercolor paper
Acrylic / Gouache paints (Midnight Blue, Sap Green, Crimson, Gold)
Metallic Gold acrylic paint or Gold Foil Leaf

steps.title: Deep Midnight Indigo Base
steps.text: Paint a smooth, solid dark midnight indigo or deep Prussian blue background across the entire canvas.

steps.title: Sketch the Kadamba Tree & Divine Postures
steps.text: Lightly trace the swirling gnarled branches of the sacred Kadamba tree and the graceful figures of royal riders / Lord Krishna.

steps.title: Layer Leaf Foliage (Kalam Stippling)
steps.text: Paint dense leaf clusters using deep emerald green, then highlight each individual leaf tip with yellow-green fine liner strokes.

steps.title: Apply Gold Leaf & Metallic Accents
steps.text: Apply gold leaf or rich metallic gold paint to the jewelry, crowns, horse saddles, halos, and royal garments.

steps.title: Pichwai Lotus Pond Border
steps.text: At the bottom and perimeter, paint blooming pink lotuses with broad emerald lily pads and swimming sacred fish.

states.name: Odisha
states.history: Pattachitra (Patta = cloth/canvas, Chitra = picture) is rooted in the 12th-century worship of Lord Jagannath at Puri. When the deities undergo their annual ritual bath (Anasara) and remain sequestered, massive Pattachitras are installed as living icons in the sanctum sanctorum.
states.significance: Raghurajpur near Puri is a designated Heritage Crafts Village where every single household preserves the Chitrakar lineage, grinding conch shells and mineral stones into indelible pigments.
facts: The canvas is prepared by pasting two layers of cotton cloth together using tamarind seed paste (Niryas kalpa) and crushed limestone.
Lines are drawn directly with the brush without any preliminary pencil sketching.
Finished paintings are passed over a charcoal fire and coated with pure tree lacquer, making them water-resistant for centuries.

tutorial.title: Painting the Sacred Shri Ram Sabha in Pattachitra Style
materials: Bright Gouache or Poster colors (Crimson, Lemon Yellow, Royal Blue, Viridian, White, Black)
Gloss varnish for traditional lacquer finish

steps.title: Construct the Characteristic Pattachitra Border
steps.text: Draw a decorative multi-tiered border around the canvas with scrolling floral vines, petals, and diamond motifs.

steps.title: Block Out Sacred Character Silhouettes
steps.text: Position Lord Rama, Devi Sita under the grand royal umbrella (Chhatra), and Lord Hanuman in devotional Anjali mudra.

steps.title: Fill with Pure Primary Pigments
steps.text: Paint Rama in divine azure blue (Neelamegha), Sita in golden turmeric yellow, and Hanuman in bright orange saffron.

steps.title: Intricate Black Linework (Ranga)
steps.text: Using your finest 00 brush with dense black ink, outline all figures, ornaments, crowns, and drapery folds.

steps.title: Add Fine White Stipples & Gloss Coat
steps.text: Add tiny white dot patterns along borders, crown jewels, and garment edges. Finish with a clear gloss coat to emulate ancient tree resin lacquer.

states.name: Sikkim
states.history: Thangkas arrived in Sikkim with Guru Padmasambhava and Tibetan Buddhist monastic traditions in the 8th century. Preserved by the lamas of Rumtek, Enchey, and Pemayangtse monasteries.
states.significance: A Thangka is not merely decorative art, but a consecrated visual meditation blueprint (Yantra). Masters must undergo strict meditative cleansing and follow sacred geometric grids (Iconometry).
facts: The proportions of the Buddha’s face, torso, and lotus throne follow exact mathematical ratios defined in the Kālachakra Tantra.
Gold details are burnished with polished cat-eye or agate stones to create matte and shiny alternating textures.
Traditionally framed in three layers of pure silk brocade symbolizing the three realms of existence.
materials: Handspun cotton sized with yak-hide glue & chalk
Crushed lapis lazuli, malachite, cinnabar minerals

tutorial.title: Painting the Shakyamuni Buddha Mandala & Lotus Throne
materials: Gouache / Acrylics (Cyan, Lapis Blue, Crimson Red, Gold, Green, Pink)

steps.title: Construct the Sacred Iconometric Grid
steps.text: Draw a central vertical plumb line (Brahmasutra) and horizontal markers. Follow standard 12-angula head proportions.

steps.title: Sketch the Lotus Petals and Radiant Halo
steps.text: Below the seated posture, sketch alternating layers of blooming lotus petals (Pink and Sky Blue). Draw a circle for the head halo and body aura.

steps.title: Apply Flat Mineral Base Tones
steps.text: Paint the sky in soft cyan blue, the halo in deep vermilion, and the Buddha’s robe in saffron and madder red.

steps.title: Facial Features & Earth-Touching Mudra
steps.text: Paint the blue Ushnisha hair curls, meditative downward-glancing eyes, and the right hand extending downwards in Bhumisparsha mudra.

steps.title: Gold Cloud Swirls & Ray Lining
steps.text: Using metallic gold, line the robe hems with intricate lotus patterns and draw fine golden rays emanating from the halo.

states.name: Karnataka
states.history: Flourished under the Wodeyar Dynasty in the cultural capital of Mysuru, particularly during the reign of Raja Wodeyar and Mummadi Krishnaraja Wodeyar in the 17th-19th centuries.
states.significance: Mysore paintings are renowned for their delicate lyricism, subtle muted color palettes, and low-relief gesso work that is less heavy than Tanjore, creating a refined classical elegance.
facts: Gesso paste (Gesso relief) is prepared using zinc oxide (white lead) and pure gum arabic applied in subtle 1mm relief.
Pure 24-karat gold leaves are pressed on the gesso and burnished so that only jewelry and thrones catch the light.
The faces are characterized by soft, rounded oval beauty, serene expressions, and realistic skin shading.
motifs: Muted Floral Arabesques with 24K Burnished Gold

tutorial.title: Creating a Mysore Style Gold-Embossed Goddess Sharada
materials: Wood panel or heavy watercolor board
3D Outliner paste or ceramic relief paste for gesso
Gold leaf foil sheets or metallic gold paint
Acrylic paints (Cream, Deep Red, Emerald, Ochre)

steps.title: Pencil Sketch on Mounted Board
steps.text: Draw the serene seated figure of Goddess Sharadamba playing the Veena, with celestial Gandharva attendants in the background.

steps.title: Apply 3D Gesso Relief on Jewelry & Arch
steps.text: Using your relief outliner, pipe delicate raised beads and lines onto the crown (Mukuta), necklaces, bracelets, and the Veena bridge.

steps.title: Apply Gold Leaf on Relief Work
steps.text: Apply gilding size glue to the raised relief, place the 24K gold leaf sheet gently, and buff away excess with a soft dry brush.

steps.title: Paint Soft Classical Tones
steps.text: Paint the body in soft sandalwood cream, the saree in pearl white with gold borders, and the background in deep Prussian slate.

steps.title: Border Framing and Sealing
steps.text: Create an embossed gold leaf border around the wooden frame and protect the work with a clear protective spray.

states.name: Tamil Nadu
states.history: Emerged in the 16th century in the Chola heartland of Thanjavur under the patronage of Nayaka and Maratha rulers (notably King Serfoji II).
states.significance: Tanjore paintings are sacred icons designed to transform living spaces into sanctified temple inner shrines (Garbhagriha). The high-relief gold and glittering gemstones catch oil-lamp light.
facts: Gesso is made from powdered unboiled limestone (Chunnam) or French chalk combined with tamarind seed gum.
Encrusted with genuine Jaipur uncut semi-precious gems (Kundan) and covered with 22K/24K gold foils (Thagadu).
The central deity is portrayed with a charming plump face, almond eyes, and nestled beneath a grand carved temple arch (Prabhavali).
materials: Jaipur glass gemstones and semi-precious rubies/emeralds
motifs: Swarna Thagadu (24K Gold Foil Filigree Relief)

tutorial.title: Crafting a Royal Tanjore Gemstone & Gold Arch Icon

steps.title: Board Preparation & Sacred Arch Sketch
steps.text: Mount cotton cloth onto your wooden board. Draw the majestic multi-pillared temple arch (Prabhavali) and the central deity.

steps.title: Embed Gemstones in Arch & Ornaments
steps.text: Press sparkling red rubies and emerald green gems into the pillar headers, crown, and temple arch contours.

steps.title: Sculpt 3D Gesso Relief (Muck Work)
steps.text: Using a cone or spatula, apply thick muck paste around the gems, building up 3mm to 5mm raised ornamental filigree.

steps.title: Affix 24K Gold Foil (Thagadu)
steps.text: Apply adhesive over the dried relief. Carefully press gold foil over the gesso, using a blunt stylus to press gold tightly into every groove.

steps.title: Coloring the Sacred Murti
steps.text: Paint the deity’s face and body with divine dark stone or glowing sandalwood hues. Paint the background in deep royal maroon.

states.name: Himachal Pradesh
states.history: Flourished in the 18th century under Maharaja Sansar Chand of Kangra in the picturesque Kangra valley, after Mughal court painters migrated to the peaceful Shivalik foothills.
states.significance: Kangra miniatures are celebrated for their romantic lyrical sensitivity, delicate depiction of women (Nayikas), lush green Himalayan landscapes, and devotion to Radha-Krishna.
facts: Artisans used natural colors derived from crushed rocks, lapis lazuli, wild flowers, and Himalayan tree saps.
The fine lines were painted using the down-hair of baby birds or single squirrel tail bristles.
Vasanta (Spring) and rainy monsoon seasons are depicted with unmatched botanical and avian precision.
motifs: Sapphire Peacocks Drinking from Lotus Springs

tutorial.title: Painting a Kangra Nayika & Blossoming Almond Orchard
materials: Watercolors or gouache (Sap Green, Turquoise, Saffron, Ultramarine Blue, Titanium White)

steps.title: Paint the Lyrical Rolling Hills
steps.text: Paint a sweeping gradient of soft Himalayan spring greens from light mint at the horizon to rich sap green in the foreground.

steps.title: Sketch the Graceful Nayika Contour
steps.text: Draw the delicate profile of the maiden with arched eyebrows, serene almond eyes, and swirling translucent odhani (veil).

steps.title: Delicate Almond Blossoms
steps.text: In the background, paint a dark slender tree branching into hundreds of tiny white and soft pink flower blossoms.

steps.title: Paint the Royal Blue Peacock
steps.text: Paint the iridescent blue peacock perched beside the maiden, tilting its head upwards to receive her pearl necklace.

steps.title: Fine Pearl & Gold Filigree
steps.text: With an ultra-fine 000 brush, paint the white pearl necklace and gold dots on the transparent royal blue veil.

states.name: Madhya Pradesh
states.history: Originated with the Gond tribe, one of the largest indigenous tribal communities in India residing in the forests of central India. Pioneered to global acclaim by legendary master Jangarh Singh Shyam.
states.significance: Gonds believe that viewing good art brings good luck (chitravans). Every natural element-trees, birds, tigers, rivers-is inhabited by a sacred spirit that is brought to life through intricate repetitive line and dot textures.
facts: Each Gond artist develops their own signature texture pattern (dots, dashes, fish scales, drops, or diagonal lines).
The Mahua tree is honored as the giver of life, shade, sweet flowers, and spirit communication.
Traditional pigments were harvested from yellow clay (Peeli mitti), black charcoal, plant sap, and red ironstone.
motifs: Mahua Tree of Life & Ancestral Spirits
Signature Tribal Dot & Line Vibration Weaves

tutorial.title: Creating a Gond Textured Sacred Tree & Dotted Wildlife
materials: Heavy drawing paper or canvas board
Acrylic or poster paints (Black, Ochre Yellow, Brick Red, Viridian Green, White)

steps.title: Draw the Fluid Organic Silhouette
steps.text: Draw the flowing trunk of the sacred Mahua tree and the stylized silhouettes of two forest animals standing beneath it.

steps.title: Fill with Flat Bold Background Blocks
steps.text: Paint the body of the animals in solid contrast blocks: one in deep charcoal black, the second in rich brick red.

steps.title: Apply Rhythmic Gond Dot Patterns
steps.text: Dip the tip of your brush or stylus in white paint and make precise, rhythmic, evenly spaced dots across the black animal body.

steps.title: Leaf Mosaic Texturing
steps.text: Inside each leaf cluster of the tree, paint tiny parallel line hatchings or small fish-scale curves.

steps.title: Vibrant Accents and Border Frame
steps.text: Add cheerful yellow dots to the red animal and frame the artwork with a simple tribal dotted border.

states.name: Gujarat
states.history: Rogan art is a rare 400-year-old Persian-origin craft preserved exclusively by the Khatri family in Nirona village, Kutch. Pithora paintings are sacred ritual murals painted by Rathwa and Bhil tribes.
states.significance: Rogan involves boiling castor seed oil for days into a sticky paste mixed with mineral pigments, drawn with a 6-inch metal stylus without touching the fabric directly. Lippan art cools desert mud huts with sparkling mirrors.
facts: Rogan paint is folded in half across the fabric to create a perfect mirror image of the complex mandala pattern.
Only a handful of master artisans in the world possess the secret of brewing the castor oil Rogan paste.
Lippan art uses clay mixed with camel dung and small geometric mirrors to reflect desert lantern light.

tutorial.title: Creating a Kutch Lippan Mud & Mirror Art Mandala
materials: Round wooden board or canvas panel
Air-dry clay or Ceramic clay dough

steps.title: Mark Geometric Concentric Rings
steps.text: Draw concentric circles radiating from the center of the wooden board with 8 symmetrical divider rays.

steps.title: Roll Fine Clay Coils (Lippan Border)
steps.text: Roll air-dry clay into smooth, uniform pencil-thin coils between your palms.

steps.title: Glue Coils onto Grid Outlines
steps.text: Apply glue along the pencil rings and press the clay coils firmly down to form 3D raised dividing ridges.

steps.title: Embed Sparkling Mirrors (Aabhla)
steps.text: Press diamond and circular craft mirrors into the spaces between clay ridges with adhesive.

steps.title: White Chalk Wash Finish
steps.text: Paint the clay ridges with crisp titanium white acrylic paint, letting the mirrors reflect light brilliantly.

states.name: West Bengal
states.history: Kalighat painting emerged in the 19th century around the Kali Temple in Kolkata, where rural scroll painters adapted to urban life by creating swift, fluid brush drawings on inexpensive paper for pilgrims.
states.significance: Famous for bold theatrical strokes, expressive satirical depictions of the Bengali Babus, and divine depictions of Goddess Kali, Durga, and Shiva with sweeping brush contours.
facts: Pioneered early modern Indian secular and satirical art alongside sacred iconography.
Shaded contours were achieved with a single sweeping brush loaded with dark pigment on one edge and water on the other.
Influenced legendary modern master Jamini Roy.

tutorial.title: Painting Goddess Durga in Expressive Kalighat Style
materials: Red, Yellow ochre, Indigo blue watercolors
Large round mop brush and detail liner brush

steps.title: Draw Sweeping Monumental Contours
steps.text: With broad, confident strokes, draw the rounded voluptuous face of Goddess Durga with large fish-shaped eyes (Meenakshi).

steps.title: Create the Signature Edge Shading
steps.text: Load a wide flat brush with pigment on one corner and clear water on the other. Trace along the jawline to create instant soft gradient shadow.

steps.title: Fill with Saturated Ochre & Madder
steps.text: Color the crown and ornaments in bright warm ochre yellow, and the saree in bold crimson vermilion.

steps.title: Add Third Eye & Sacred Alpona Details
steps.text: Paint the prominent vertical third eye on the forehead and decorate with traditional red bindi dots.

steps.title: Final Expressive Ink Linework
steps.text: Sharpen eyebrows, nose ridge, and jewelry with clean black ink lines.

states.name: Kerala
states.history: Kerala murals adorn the walls of ancient temples and palaces like Padmanabhapuram, Mattancherry, and Guruvayur, dating between the 9th and 18th centuries CE.
states.significance: Depicts scenes from the Dhyana Shlokas using the Panchavarna (five sacred natural colors: Red, Yellow, Green, Blue/Black, White) following ancient Natyashastra stances.
facts: Artisans use the white lime plaster on laterite temple walls as the natural white color without adding white paint.
Characters are categorized into Sattvika (divine green), Rajasika (royal red/yellow), and Tamasika (dark blue/black).
The eyes are painted in a sacred concluding ritual called Nayanonmeelanam (Opening of the Eyes).
motifs: Sattvika Divine Green & Panchavarna Sacred Palette

tutorial.title: Painting a Divine Sattvika Krishna in Kerala Mural Style
materials: Panchavarna acrylic colors (Yellow Ochre, Indian Red, Sap Green, Ivory, Black)

steps.title: Sketch the Classical Stance (Tribhanga)
steps.text: Draw Lord Krishna in the poised three-bend Tribhanga posture playing the flute, surrounded by ornamental temple arches.

steps.title: Yellow Base Layer (Kavippu)
steps.text: Paint the entire figure in a base coat of warm yellow ochre, which serves as the luminous undertone for all colors.

steps.title: Apply Sattvika Green for Divine Skin
steps.text: Layer rich emerald green over the skin areas, leaving ornaments and garlands in yellow.

steps.title: Indian Red & Terracotta Shading
steps.text: Shade the outlines, drapery folds, and crowns with deep Indian red terracotta tones.

steps.title: Nayanonmeelanam (Painting the Divine Eyes)
steps.text: Paint the large expressive eyes with white sclera, sharp black pupils, and curved black eyebrows.

states.name: Punjab
states.artForm: Phulkari Floral Silk Embroidery & Mud Wall Art
states.history: Phulkari ("flower craft") has been referenced in the 18th-century Punjabi epic Heer Ranjha. Embroidered by mothers and grandmothers on home-spun khaddar fabric as heirlooms for brides.
states.significance: Every stitch is counted on the reverse side of coarse cotton cloth using untwisted pure silk floss (Pat). Bagh (garden) Phulkaris cover the entire fabric so no base cloth is visible.
facts: Embroidered from the back of the cloth using the darning stitch, requiring intense spatial memory.
Sainchi Phulkari depicts rural scenes: spinning wheels (charkha), birds, village jewelry, and weddings.
Traditionally gifted during the birth of a child and worn at wedding ceremonies.
motifs: Pat Silk Lustrous Thread Floss Weaves

tutorial.title: Designing a Geometric Phulkari / Bagh Floral Pattern
materials: Gouache/Acrylic paints (Saffron, Hot Pink, Mustard Yellow, Turquoise, Gold)

steps.title: Draw the Diamond Geometric Grid
steps.text: Draw a grid of interlocking diamond shapes across your canvas. Phulkari relies on precise geometric symmetry.

steps.title: Fill with Untwisted Silk Floss Effect
steps.text: Paint parallel diagonal strokes within each diamond facet using vibrant saffron orange and hot magenta pink.

steps.title: Alternate Contrasting Color Facets
steps.text: Fill adjacent diamonds with bright mustard yellow and turquoise blue to create dazzling visual vibration.

steps.title: Add Corner Peacocks and Paisley Motifs
steps.text: In the four corners of your design, paint stylized geometric peacocks with fanned tail feathers made of stepped triangles.

steps.title: Nazar Battu (Deliberate Flaw for Protection)
steps.text: Leave one small petal in a different color (e.g. blue instead of pink) as the traditional Nazar Battu to ward off the evil eye.

states.name: Telangana
states.history: Cheriyal scrolls flourished in Telangana for over 400 years as continuous narrative cloth scrolls up to 40 feet long, sung by traveling storytellers (Kaki Padagollu) in rural villages.
states.significance: Cheriyal art uses vibrant red background canvases and stylized theatrical characters with bulbous eyes, vivid costumes, and comic expressions illustrating folk legends.
facts: Canvas is prepared by applying Khadi cloth treated with tamarind seed paste, white mud, and tree gum.
Accompanied by handmade 3D Cheriyal masks crafted from sawdust and tamarind paste.
Received prestigious Geographical Indication (GI) protection.

tutorial.title: Painting a Cheriyal Folk Narrative Panel with Red Backdrop
materials: Bright Red, White, Ochre, Green, Black acrylic paints

steps.title: Bright Vermilion Red Background
steps.text: Paint the entire canvas with a flat, vibrant scarlet or vermilion red background coat.

steps.title: Draw Stylized Folk Figures
steps.text: Sketch village figures with round heads, sharp prominent noses, and large wide-open staring eyes.

steps.title: Color Traditional Attires
steps.text: Paint traditional sarees and dhotis in yellow ochre, emerald green, and white borders.

steps.title: Bold Black Inking
steps.text: Outline every figure, muscle contour, and facial expression with crisp, bold black outlines.

steps.title: Add Floral Story Dividers
steps.text: Paint vertical divider panels of four-petaled white flowers to separate narrative episodes.

states.name: Arunachal Pradesh
states.history: The Monpa people of the Tawang and West Kameng region follow Tibetan Buddhism, and their monasteries are centres for thangka painting, mask making and wood carving. Monpa handmade paper has long been used for scriptures.
states.significance: Monpa art carries Buddhist teaching and is used in monastery festivals, where masked dances tell moral stories.
facts: Tawang Monastery is the largest monastery in India.
Arunachal Pradesh is home to more than 25 major tribal communities, each with its own crafts.
materials: Cotton cloth stretched on a frame

steps.title: Mark a border
steps.text: Rule a frame about 2 cm inside the paper edge.

steps.title: Draw lotus petals
steps.text: Repeat a row of simple pointed petals along the frame.

steps.title: Colour boldly
steps.text: Use flat red, blue, yellow and green, then outline in black.

states.name: Assam
states.history: Assam has an old tradition of silk. Muga, a naturally golden silk produced only in Assam, was historically woven for royalty, and the town of Sualkuchi on the Brahmaputra is its main weaving centre.
states.significance: Muga silk and the red-bordered gamosa are symbols of Assamese identity and are given as marks of respect.
facts: Muga silk has a Geographical Indication (GI) tag.
Sualkuchi is often called the Manchester of the East.
materials: Muga, Eri and Pat silk yarn

steps.title: Plan the strip
steps.text: Divide a long strip into a white centre and two red edges.

steps.title: Add woven motifs
steps.text: Draw small flowers and diamonds along the red edges.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Colour neatly and leave short fringe cuts at both ends.

states.name: Chhattisgarh
states.history: Dhokra is a lost-wax method of casting brass and bronze that tribal artisans of the Bastar region have practised for generations. A clay core is covered in wax threads, coated in clay, then heated so molten metal replaces the wax.
states.significance: Dhokra figures of animals, deities and village life are made for rituals and homes, and each piece is one of a kind because the mould is broken to release it.
facts: Dhokra uses the lost-wax technique, one of the oldest metal casting methods.
Every cast piece is unique because its mould is destroyed.

steps.title: Shape the core
steps.text: Form a small animal from clay.

steps.title: Add cord texture
steps.text: Press thin cord coils over the surface to mimic wax threads.

steps.title: Paint
steps.text: Dry, then paint in brass tone and rub off a little for an aged look.

states.name: Goa
states.history: Goa blends Indian and Portuguese influences. Kunbi weavers made simple red and white checked cloth for village women, and a revival now brings the pattern into modern sarees.
states.significance: Kunbi checks and clay figures reflect Goa's village life and festivals.
facts: Kunbi fabric is traditionally woven in a red and white check.
Coconut palms supply shell, fibre and wood for many Goan crafts.

steps.title: Rule a grid
steps.text: Draw light squares of equal size.

steps.title: Paint bands
steps.text: Paint alternate horizontal and vertical red bands.

steps.title: Overlap
steps.text: Let crossings darken to give the woven look.

states.name: Haryana
states.history: Panipat is a historic weaving town, known for handloom khes, durries and woven furnishings, using cotton and recycled yarn.
states.significance: Weaving and clay crafts here are part of daily and festival life, from woven bedding to Sanjhi wall figures.
facts: Panipat is nicknamed the City of Weavers.
Sanjhi is a festival wall art made by girls in northern India.

steps.title: Cut the warp
steps.text: Cut parallel slits in a sheet.

steps.title: Weave strips
steps.text: Pass colour strips over and under.

steps.title: Pattern
steps.text: Alternate colours to make stripes and borders.

states.name: Jharkhand
states.history: Sohrai is painted on village mud walls during the harvest festival, and Khovar is painted in wedding rooms. Women of the Hazaribagh region create them with natural earth colours.
states.significance: These paintings celebrate harvest, cattle and marriage, and renew the walls each year.
facts: Sohrai-Khovar painting has a GI tag.
Brushes are often twigs, chewed sticks or fingers.

steps.title: Cover the base
steps.text: Colour paper with a thin red-brown wash.

steps.title: Draw the animal
steps.text: Paint a bold outline of a bull or deer in white.

steps.title: Add pattern
steps.text: Fill the body with dots and combs.

states.name: Manipur
states.artForm: Longpi Black Pottery & Moirang Phee Weaving
states.history: Longpi pottery from Ukhrul is shaped by hand without a wheel from local stone and clay and fired to a deep black. Moirang phee is a traditional Meitei textile.
states.significance: These crafts keep the techniques of the Tangkhul Naga and Meitei communities alive.
facts: Longpi pottery uses crushed stone mixed with clay.
Loktak Lake, with its floating phumdis, is a famous natural site in Manipur.

steps.title: Make coils
steps.text: Roll long thin clay ropes.

steps.title: Build up
steps.text: Coil and smooth them into a small pot.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Dry, then paint black.

states.name: Meghalaya
states.history: The Khasi, Garo and Jaintia peoples use cane and bamboo from their forests for baskets, mats and hats. Eri silk, called Ryndia, is spun from silkworms fed on castor leaves.
states.significance: Craft and landscape are closely linked, as in the living root bridges grown by Khasi communities.
facts: Living root bridges are shaped from rubber fig roots over many years.
Eri silk is sometimes called ahimsa silk, as the moth can emerge before the cocoon is spun.

steps.title: Cut strips
steps.text: Cut equal strips.

steps.title: Weave a base
steps.text: Cross strips over and under.

steps.title: Raise sides
steps.text: Fold up and glue a rim.

states.name: Mizoram
states.history: The puan is a wrap-around cloth woven by Mizo women on a backstrap loom. Puanchei, in red, black, green and white, is worn at festivals and weddings.
states.significance: Puans mark identity and celebration, and bamboo is central to daily life in the hills.
facts: Mizoram has one of the highest literacy rates among Indian states.
Bamboo covers a large share of the state's forest.

steps.title: Choose colours
steps.text: Pick red, black, green and white.

steps.title: Draw bands
steps.text: Fill the strip with horizontal bands.

steps.title: Add zigzag
steps.text: Draw a zigzag band between stripes.

states.name: Nagaland
states.history: Naga communities weave distinctive shawls on backstrap looms. Patterns and colours identify the tribe and the status of the wearer.
states.significance: Shawls, woodwork and beads mark identity, achievement and festivals such as the Hornbill Festival in Kohima.
facts: Each Naga tribe has its own shawl designs.
The mithun is the state animal.

steps.title: Colour base
steps.text: Fill the strip with a dark base.

steps.title: Add bands
steps.text: Draw white and red bands.

steps.title: Motif
steps.text: Place a mithun or spear symbol in the centre.

states.name: Tripura
states.history: Bamboo and cane are abundant in Tripura, and artisans make furniture, baskets and decorative items. Tripuri women weave risa and pachra on backstrap looms.
states.significance: Bamboo craft is a livelihood for many families and is closely linked to Tripuri identity.
facts: Tripura has a large tribal population with several communities.
Risa is a traditional Tripuri textile.

steps.title: Prepare strips
steps.text: Cut strips of two colours.

steps.title: Weave
steps.text: Weave them in a diagonal twill.

steps.title: Glue
steps.text: Glue the edges.

states.name: Uttarakhand
states.history: Aipan is a ritual art of Kumaon. Women draw patterns in white rice paste on a red base of geru earth on floors, walls and thresholds, especially at festivals.
states.significance: Aipan is drawn to welcome deities and bring prosperity.
facts: The white colour is made of rice paste (bisvar).
The red base is geru, a red earth.

steps.title: Red base
steps.text: Cover a sheet in red.

steps.title: Draw lines
steps.text: Use your finger to draw a border.

steps.title: Add symbols
steps.text: Draw a lotus in the centre.

states.name: Uttar Pradesh
states.history: Chikankari is a white-thread embroidery of Lucknow, traditionally on fine cotton or muslin, using stitches such as shadow work and stem stitch.
states.significance: It is one of the best-known Indian textile crafts and supports many women artisans.
facts: Lucknow Chikankari has a GI tag.
Banarasi brocade is woven in Varanasi.

steps.title: Mark a design
steps.text: Draw a simple vine in pencil.

steps.title: Stem stitch
steps.text: Sew along the line in overlapping stitches.

steps.title: Add leaves
steps.text: Fill small leaves with tiny stitches.

states.name: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
states.history: Island communities use shell, coconut and drift wood for ornaments and tools. Some protected shells and corals may not be collected or sold, so buy from licensed emporiums.
states.significance: Crafts follow the sea and forest, and reflect the islands' ecology.
facts: Collecting protected marine species is illegal.
The islands include indigenous communities that are legally protected.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Press clay into a shell form.

steps.title: Texture
steps.text: Scratch ridges.

steps.title: String
steps.text: Make a hole and thread the cord.

states.name: Chandigarh
states.artForm: Nek Chand Rock Garden Waste Sculpture
states.history: Nek Chand, a road inspector, began building the Rock Garden in 1957 from discarded urban and industrial waste, first in secret. It grew into a sculpture park.
states.significance: It shows how waste can become folk art.
facts: The garden has thousands of figures made from waste.
Chandigarh was planned by Le Corbusier.

steps.title: Sketch
steps.text: Draw a figure.

steps.title: Sort
steps.text: Sort pieces by colour.

steps.title: Glue
steps.text: Glue pieces in place.

states.name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
states.history: Tribal communities such as the Varli, Kokna and Dhodia use bamboo for baskets, mats and household items, and Varli families paint ritual wall art.
states.significance: Craft and ritual are part of daily life and festivals.
facts: The territory was formed by merging two UTs in 2020.
Varli painting is also found in Maharashtra.

steps.title: Triangles
steps.text: Draw two triangles for a body.

steps.title: Limbs
steps.text: Add stick limbs.

steps.title: Dance
steps.text: Link figures into a circle.

states.name: Delhi
states.history: Zardozi is metal-thread embroidery of gold or silver thread, sequins and beads, brought to prominence in the Mughal courts.
states.significance: It is used for bridal and ceremonial clothing.
facts: Zar means gold and dozi means embroidery.
Delhi has been a centre of Mughal craft.

steps.title: Draw
steps.text: Mark a flower.

steps.title: Outline
steps.text: Couch gold thread.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Sew beads in the centre.

states.name: Jammu and Kashmir
states.history: Kani shawls are woven with small wooden bobbins called kanis, producing intricate patterns. Papier-mache is made from pulped paper that is moulded, painted and varnished.
states.significance: These crafts are central to Kashmiri identity and livelihood.
facts: Kani shawls can take months to weave.
Kashmir is known for carpets and walnut wood.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: Paste strips onto the bowl.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Let dry and remove.

steps.title: Paint
steps.text: Paint a floral pattern.

states.name: Ladakh
states.history: Ladakh is home to Buddhist monasteries that train thangka painters. The Changthang plateau is known for its pashmina goats.
states.significance: Thangkas support religious practice, and pashmina supports herders.
facts: Pashmina is combed from goats in the Changthang region.
Perak is a traditional turquoise headdress.

steps.title: Circle
steps.text: Draw concentric circles.

steps.title: Divide
steps.text: Divide into eight parts.

steps.title: Colour
steps.text: Fill symmetrically.

states.name: Lakshadweep
states.history: Coconut is central to island life, and coir fibre is spun and twisted into rope and mats. Shells and coconut shells are used for ornaments.
states.significance: Crafts show how islanders use local resources.
facts: Coir is fibre from coconut husk.
Most islands are coral atolls.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Cut three strands.

steps.title: Braid
steps.text: Braid tightly.

steps.title: Tie
steps.text: Knot the ends.

states.name: Puducherry
states.history: Puducherry has a mix of French and Tamil heritage. Handmade paper is made in the Sri Aurobindo Ashram, and Auroville has many craft units.
states.significance: Crafts here blend sustainable practice and design.
facts: Handmade paper is made from cotton rags.
Auroville was founded in 1968.

steps.title: Pulp
steps.text: Blend torn paper.

steps.title: Pour
steps.text: Spread on a screen.

steps.title: Dry
steps.text: Press and dry.

tours.title: Mithila Sacred Canvas: Madhubani Heritage & Village Trail
tours.theme: Folk Wall Murals, Natural Pigments & Kohbar Traditions
highlights: Private session with National Awardee Mithila masters in Ranti & Jitwarpur
Hands-on workshop extracting natural yellow from turmeric and blue from aparajita
Walk through village mud homes adorned with Kohbar fertility marriage murals
Authentic Maithili culinary lunch (Litti Chokha & Makhana Kheer)
tips: Nearest Railway Station: Madhubani / Darbhanga Airport (35 km)
Best Months: October to March when village walls are freshly painted after monsoon
Artisan Etiquette: Always ask permission before photographing family Kohbar bedrooms
Souvenir Buying: Buy directly from registered women artisan self-help groups (SHGs) with GI authenticity seals

tours.title: The Sacred Pen: Srikalahasti Kalamkari & Temple Scroll Expedition
tours.theme: Organic Dyes, Swarnamukhi River Alchemy & Epic Temple Hangings
highlights: Witness the 17-step river washing and natural myrobalan mordant process
Hold the traditional bamboo-and-sheep-wool Kalam pen used for 600 years
Exclusive viewing of ancient Vijayanagara era temple scrolls at Srikalahasti
Learn how buffalo milk prevents natural madder dye from bleeding on cotton
tips: Nearest Major Hub: Tirupati (38 km) / Chennai Airport (110 km)
What to Wear: Breathable cotton clothing suitable for walking near riverbanks
Photography: Permitted in artisan workshops; avoid flash in temple sanctums
Craft Verification: Srikalahasti style is 100% freehand pen work; distinct from Machilipatnam block print

tours.title: Echoes of the Sahyadri: Warli Tribal Forest & Sacred Canvas Trail
tours.theme: Neolithic Geometry, Rice Flour Murals & the Cosmic Tarpa Dance
highlights: Visit ancestral tribal hamlets in Dahanu and Jawhar nested in the Sahyadris
Learn the ancient Warli human figure construction using intersecting balance triangles
Listen to live hypnotic Tarpa trumpet music during a twilight village circle dance
Cook organic Nachni (finger millet) bhakri on village earthen stoves
tips: Nearest Railway Station: Dahanu Road / Mumbai (120 km)
Recommended Gear: Comfortable walking shoes for rustic red-earth village trails
Respectful Conduct: Warli culture is egalitarian and nature-worshipping; preserve village cleanliness
Authenticity Check: True Warli uses rice paste on mud/geru background without bright chemical pigments

tours.title: Divine Splendor: Nathdwara Pichwai & Royal Mewar Miniature Trail
tours.theme: 24K Gold Leaf, Lapis Lazuli, Sacred Kadamba Trees & Temple Backdrops
highlights: Visit 400-year-old Chitron Ki Gali (Street of Painters) in temple town Nathdwara
Observe grinding of pure lapis lazuli, malachite, and 24-karat gold leaf
Learn the squirrel-hair miniature brush control technique for micro-details
Mewari royal lunch overlooking Lake Pichola / Aravalli hills
tips: Nearest Airport: Maharana Pratap Airport Udaipur (45 km)
Best Time to Visit: Sharad Purnima or Janmashtami when Pichwais are changed for every festival
Artisan Etiquette: Remove footwear before entering traditional painter havelis
Buying Guide: Look for smooth burnished gold leaf that catches natural sunlight with warm yellow luster

tours.title: The Eternal Scroll: Raghurajpur Heritage Craft Village & Puri Trail
tours.theme: Conch Shell White, Palm-Leaf Etchings & Jagannath Devotional Art
highlights: Spend a full day in Raghurajpur where every single home is an open art gallery
Etch intricate Tala Pattachitra using an iron stylus on dried palm leaves
Watch conch shells ground with tamarind seeds to create glowing white pigment
Witness an authentic Gotipua acrobatic temple dance performance
tips: Nearest Major Station: Puri (14 km) / Bhubaneswar Airport (50 km)
Village Courtesy: Walk leisurely through both village streets; every family welcomes guests with warmth
Palm Leaf Care: Keep palm-leaf scrolls away from excessive moisture to preserve lampblack inking
Authenticity Seal: Ensure your Pattachitra is painted on pure tamarind-cloth canvas or palm fronds
